- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤0.33) or shows sharp reversal (e.g., -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for mean reversion or short-term rebound.
- After a price spike (forecast > true outcome by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in subsequent periods; dampen forecast by 2–5% for 2–3 periods ahead.
- If sentiment is mixed or trending sideways (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–2% downward adjustment if price has been above 30-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag by 1–2 days in reaction to sentiment shifts; adjust forecast to align with sentiment peak or trough 1–2 days earlier.
- When sentiment history shows repeated high/low extremes (e.g., 1.00 followed by -0.33), model overreacts; apply smoothing filter to reduce volatility in forecast.
